synopsis: Independent test-plan review means reviewers who neither wrote the plan nor need it to succeed examine its scope, methods, metrics and thresholds before testing; thresholds must be fixed before results are seen [f14988, f14992]. Across Chapters 1, 12 and 13, the recommendation is to embed independence early, review the plan before prototype safety testing, and build a measured, independently reviewed credibility envelope before the prototype arrives [f741, f10356, f10466]. Review should cover data separation, physical confirmation, scenario coverage and the validity envelope, while skeptical reviewers challenge assumptions, acceptance thresholds, integration dependencies and evidence independence [f14991, f9962]. Scheduling requires early agreement on the assessment counterpart and review criteria, and a safety/legal dry run should produce written comments on a representative evidence package months before launch; review queues can become the critical path [f8245, f10964, f14998]. The corpus presents independent review as a practice- and standards-supported safeguard, not a proven cure: it cannot rescue incomplete engineering late, and the booklet found no evidence that red teams improve engineering outcomes [f15001, f1056, f15000].
